detection_checks.windows_is_set_up_to_sa: Windows is set up to save a dump at every blue screen: that is what lets Dump Finder name the faulty driver.

knowledge_base.amd_driver_timeout_driver: AMD Driver Timeout ('Driver timeout has occurred' / amdwddmg)
knowledge_base.3_10s_black_screen_amd_bu: 3–10s black screen, AMD Bug Report popup, game/browser crash, or Adrenalin refusing to launch ('driver version does not match').
knowledge_base.top_3_causes_1_windows_up: Top 3 causes: (1) Windows Update silently overwrites Adrenalin with an older generic driver, (2) ULPS drops idle voltage too low, (3) Windows MPO conflicts with Chrome/Discord.
knowledge_base.in_fixes_lock_gpu_driver_: In 'Fixes', lock GPU driver updates from Windows Update, disable ULPS, disable MPO, and raise TDR timeout to 10s.
knowledge_base.boot_grey_screen_in_game_: Boot Grey Screen & In-Game Adrenalin Timeout (RX 7800 XT / 7900)
knowledge_base.solid_grey_screen_when_bo: Solid grey screen when booting into Windows, plus freezes and 'AMD Adrenalin Driver Timeout' popups under heavy 3D gaming load.
knowledge_base.at_boot_windows_fast_star: At boot: Windows Fast Startup + ULPS corrupt RDNA 3 display init. In games on RX 7800 XT: a single daisy-chained 8-pin PCIe cable drooping under 400W spikes, Win11 24H2 HAGS, or factory Boost spiking >2750 MHz.
knowledge_base.1_in_fixes_disable_fast_s: 1) In 'Fixes', disable Fast Startup, ULPS, MPO, HAGS, and Issue Detection. 2) Run 2 separate 8-pin PCIe cables from the PSU (no pigtail). 3) In Adrenalin Tuning, cap Max Frequency to ~2450–2500 MHz.
knowledge_base.black_screen_100_gpu_fans: Black Screen + 100% GPU Fans + Reboot (nvlddmkm Event 153 / 0x00000116)
knowledge_base.sudden_loss_of_display_si: Sudden loss of display signal, GPU fans spinning at 100% emergency speed, audio continuing briefly, followed by a reboot.
knowledge_base.during_chrome_youtube_vid: During Chrome/YouTube video playback, Skia Graphite + MPO stalls Direct3D 11 at low P-states. An MSI Afterburner UV curve shifted too high across 750–850 mV also triggers crashes outside games.
knowledge_base.disable_mpo_skia_graphite: Disable MPO + Skia Graphite + set TdrDelay = 10s in 'Fixes', and keep your 750–850 mV curve points close to stock in MSI Afterburner.
knowledge_base.total_system_freezes_nvme: Total System Freezes & NVMe SSD Dropouts on Windows 11 (stornvme 129 / 0xEF)
knowledge_base.system_hangs_for_10_30_se: System hangs for 10–30 seconds, occasionally ending in CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED (0xEF) or KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR (0x7A).
knowledge_base.host_memory_buffer_hmb_al: Host Memory Buffer (HMB) allocation bug on Windows 11 24H2+ with DRAM-less NVMe drives (WD SN770, SN580, Lexar, Maxio) or aggressive PCIe ASPM.
knowledge_base.apply_the_nvme_hmb_stabil: Apply the 'NVMe HMB Stabilization' and 'Disable PCIe ASPM' fixes, and check for SSD firmware updates.
knowledge_base.instant_idle_reboot_on_am: Instant Idle Reboot on AMD Ryzen CPUs (WHEA-Logger Event 18)
knowledge_base.pc_reboots_abruptly_with_: PC reboots abruptly with no BSOD and no fan spin-up, almost always while idling or browsing lightly.
knowledge_base.insufficient_cpu_core_vol: Insufficient CPU core voltage during idle C-state transitions caused by an overly negative PBO Curve Optimizer (e.g., -30 all-core).
knowledge_base.in_bios_relax_curve_optim: In BIOS, relax Curve Optimizer (e.g., -15 instead of -30 on the reported APIC core) and set Power Supply Idle Control to Typical Current Idle.
knowledge_base.out_of_video_memory_shade: 'Out of Video Memory' Shader Compilation Crash (Intel 13th / 14th Gen)
knowledge_base.unreal_engine_5_games_cra: Unreal Engine 5 games crash during shader compilation with a misleading 'Out of video memory' popup or 0xc0000005 error.
knowledge_base.cpu_instability_vmin_shif: CPU instability (Vmin Shift / unlocked motherboard power limits) triggered during heavy AVX shader decompression on 13th/14th Gen i7/i9.
knowledge_base.update_motherboard_bios_m: Update motherboard BIOS (microcode 0x12F+) and enable the 'Intel Default Settings' profile in BIOS.
knowledge_base.stutters_usb_audio_crackl: Stutters, USB Audio Crackles & PCIe Drops in ITX Cases (WHEA 17)
knowledge_base.floods_of_whea_event_17_w: Floods of WHEA Event 17 warnings in Event Viewer, FPS micro-stutters, or sudden GPU disconnects.
knowledge_base.signal_loss_across_a_pcie: Signal loss across a PCIe riser cable when the motherboard negotiates PCIe Gen 5 over a Gen 4 riser (or Gen 4 over Gen 3).
knowledge_base.disable_pcie_aspm_in_fixe: Disable PCIe ASPM in 'Fixes' and manually set PCIEX16 speed to 'Gen 4' (instead of Auto) in BIOS.
knowledge_base.random_crashes_to_desktop: Random Crashes to Desktop & Memory BSODs (0x1A / 0x3B / Event 2004)
knowledge_base.games_closing_silently_af: Games closing silently after 20–40 min, browser tab crashes, or Windows Resource-Exhaustion Event 2004.
knowledge_base.manually_disabled_windows: Manually disabled Windows Pagefile, or DDR5 XMP/EXPO instability once GPU heat warms RAM sticks above 50°C.
knowledge_base.enable_automatic_windows_: Enable 'Automatic Windows Pagefile' and run the 'DISM + SFC System Check' in the Fixes tab.
knowledge_base.instant_power_off_under_h: Instant Power-Off Under Heavy 3D Load (Kernel-Power 41 with Zero Minidump)
knowledge_base.pc_clicks_off_like_a_powe: PC clicks off like a power outage during heavy 3D gaming transitions, leaving zero files in C:\Windows\Minidump.
knowledge_base.psu_protection_trip_ocp_o: PSU protection trip (OCP/OPP) from GPU transient spikes, unseated 12V-2x6 plug, or daisy-chained PCIe power cable.
knowledge_base.check_gpu_power_plug_seat: Check GPU power plug seating, use separate PSU cables per connector, and validate using the 'Stress Test' tab.
knowledge_base.idle_black_screens_severe: Idle Black Screens & Severe Stutters on Intel Arc GPUs (A & B Series)
knowledge_base.black_screen_when_waking_: Black screen when waking displays (igdkmdnd64.sys), halved FPS, or DirectX 12 TDR timeouts.
knowledge_base.intel_arc_hardware_strict: Intel Arc hardware strictly requires Resizable BAR, and aggressive PCIe ASPM L1 substates cause wake lockups on many motherboards.
knowledge_base.enable_above_4g_decoding_: Enable Above 4G Decoding + Resizable BAR in BIOS, and disable PCIe ASPM + set TdrDelay = 10s in 'Fixes'.
knowledge_base.login_bsod_memory_managem: Login BSOD MEMORY_MANAGEMENT (0x1A) on AMD Ryzen AM5 DDR5
knowledge_base.0x1a_or_0x0a_bsod_within_: 0x1A or 0x0A BSOD within 60 seconds of a fast boot on Ryzen 7000 / 9000 systems.
knowledge_base.memory_context_restore_is: 'Memory Context Restore' is enabled in BIOS while 'Power Down Enable' is left Disabled or Auto, desynchronizing the DDR5 PHY.
knowledge_base.in_bios_explicitly_set_bo: In BIOS, explicitly set BOTH Memory Context Restore AND Power Down Enable to Enabled (or both Disabled).
knowledge_base.realtek_2_5gbe_mediatek_r: Realtek 2.5GbE / MediaTek RZ616 Freezes & Anti-Cheat BSODs (vgk.sys / EAC)
knowledge_base.micro_freezes_with_ethern: Micro-freezes with Ethernet/Bluetooth dropouts (NDIS 10400 / mtkwl6ex.sys), or 0x139 BSOD launching Valorant / EAC games on Win11 24H2.
knowledge_base.buggy_eee_green_ethernet_: Buggy EEE / Green Ethernet on Realtek 2.5GbE, PCIe sleep on MediaTek RZ616, or Ring-0 Anti-Cheat colliding with Kernel Shadow Stacks / Auto HDR.
knowledge_base.apply_the_disable_2_5gbe_: Apply the 'Disable 2.5GbE EEE & Wi-Fi Power-Save' + 'Fast Startup Off' fixes, and check the Health & Conflicts tab.
knowledge_base.games_freezing_closing_or: Games freezing, closing or rebooting the PC (inpoutx64 driver from RGB software, 2026)
knowledge_base.since_the_august_2026_upd: Since the August 2026 update (KB5121003): frozen game, silent closure or EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xc0000005), sometimes a PC restart — notably ARC Raiders, The Finals or MARVEL Tōkon.
knowledge_base.microsoft_confirmed_the_c: Microsoft confirmed the cause is the inpoutx64.sys driver installed by RGB and monitoring software, not the update itself. The September 2026 updates block it automatically, except on company-managed PCs.
knowledge_base.install_the_latest_window: Install the latest Windows updates. If the driver is still loaded, disable it under 'Fixes' (Disable the inpoutx64.sys driver): that is the official workaround. RGB control may stop working until the software is updated.
knowledge_base.rtx_50_black_screens_pull: RTX 50: black screens, pulled drivers and the 12V-2x6 connector
knowledge_base.black_screen_with_fans_ra: Black screen with fans ramping up, bursts of nvlddmkm 153 events then a 0x116 blue screen (VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE), or a hard shutdown under load.
knowledge_base.three_leads_1_faulty_driv: Three leads: (1) faulty driver releases (595.59 was pulled in February 2026; 621.01 caused video freezes fixed by 621.12); (2) the PCIe Gen5 link on some motherboards; (3) on RTX 5090/5080, a badly seated 12V-2x6 connector or an adapter, which can heat up until it melts.
knowledge_base.check_the_driver_version_: Check the driver version under 'Hardware › Conflicts' and install a recent driver (with DDU if in doubt). If black screens persist on a PCIe 5.0 motherboard, force the slot to Gen4 in the BIOS (a common, unofficial workaround). With the PC off, make sure the 12V-2x6 cable is fully inserted, with no adapter and no tight bend near the card.
knowledge_base.ryzen_9000_9800x3d_instab: Ryzen 9000 / 9800X3D: instability, EXPO and motherboard BIOS
knowledge_base.pc_that_no_longer_boots_o: PC that no longer boots or boot-loops, memory blue screens (0x1A, 0x50), WHEA errors, or miscalculations during the stability test.
knowledge_base.expo_profiles_too_ambitio: EXPO profiles too ambitious for the memory controller, overly aggressive PBO or Curve Optimizer and, on some motherboards (ASRock in particular), BIOSes exceeding AMD's electrical limits: CPUs were damaged as late as 2026.
knowledge_base.update_the_motherboard_bi: Update the motherboard BIOS. Test with EXPO off first, then turn it back on; lower its frequency one step if needed. Run the 'core by core' stability test: it names the cores whose Curve Optimizer value is too negative.
knowledge_base.blue_screen_with_no_minid: Blue screen with no minidump (Kernel-Power 41 only, volmgr 161)
knowledge_base.the_pc_restarts_or_shows_: The PC restarts or shows a blue screen, but no file appears in C:\Windows\Minidump; the log only shows a Kernel-Power 41, sometimes a volmgr 161.
knowledge_base.windows_writes_the_dump_t: Windows writes the dump through the page file: if it is disabled, too small or on another drive, or if dump writing is turned off, nothing is saved. A hard power cut (power supply protection tripping) leaves no dump either.
knowledge_base.under_hardware_conflicts_: Under 'Hardware › Conflicts', check 'Blue screen recording' and apply the suggested fix (automatic page file or dumps turned back on). If everything is fine and still no dump appears, suspect the power supply: a shutdown without a blue screen is often its protection tripping.

system_health_scanner.1_dram_less_ssds_k:
1. DRAM-less SSDs (Kingston NV2/NV3, WD SN770/SN580, Crucial P3, Lexar NM790) borrow host RAM via the Host Memory Buffer (HMB) protocol.
2. On Windows 11 24H2+, a stornvme.sys bug allocates up to 200MB instead of 64MB, triggering stornvme freezes and BSODs.
3. 'Stabilize NVMe HMB' sets Microsoft's recommended HmbAllocationPolicy = 2 to cap buffer size to 64MB.
4. Check for NVMe firmware updates using the drive maker's official utility.

system_health_scanner.1_discord_user_set:
1. Discord: User Settings ⚙ > Game Overlay > Turn off 'Enable in-game overlay'.
2. Steam: Steam Settings > In-Game > Uncheck 'Enable the Steam Overlay while in-game'.
3. NVIDIA App / GeForce Experience: Settings ⚙ > Features > Disable 'In-Game Overlay' (Alt+Z).
4. RivaTuner (RTSS): Set hook level to 'Low' to prevent DirectX 12 hook collisions.
💡 Stacking multiple graphics hooks causes D3D12/Vulkan driver crashes on Alt-Tab.

engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_touche: A driver touched a memory address it was not allowed to at that moment. Almost always a third-party driver (network, audio, RGB, antivirus); less often unstable RAM.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_kernel_memory: A kernel memory block was corrupted. Typical causes: a faulty third-party driver (antivirus, VPN, RGB) or unstable RAM (XMP/EXPO profile).
engine.bug_check_catalog.windows_memory_: Windows' memory manager found a serious inconsistency. Very often RAM (aggressive XMP/EXPO profile, failing stick), sometimes a driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_kernel_compon: A kernel component (driver) raised an error it did not handle. Parameter 2 points straight into the faulting driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_ntfs_file_s: The NTFS file system hit an error: failing disk, faulty SATA cable or volume corruption. Run chkdsk and check SMART.
engine.bug_check_catalog.an_error_occurr: An error occurred during a system call. Parameter 2 is the faulting instruction, often in a graphics driver, anti-cheat or antivirus.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_page_frame_: The page frame database is corrupted. Most often unstable or failing RAM; more rarely a driver freeing the same memory twice.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_kernel_acce: The kernel accessed memory that does not exist. Parameter 3 points to the faulting instruction. Causes: buggy driver, antivirus, or unstable RAM.
engine.bug_check_catalog.windows_could_n: Windows could not read back a kernel memory page from disk. Sign of a failing SSD/disk, cable or unstable controller.
engine.bug_check_catalog.windows_cannot_: Windows cannot reach its boot disk: SATA/RAID mode changed in BIOS, failed storage driver update or failing disk.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_system_thread: A system thread crashed and was not caught. Parameter 2 points into the responsible driver (often graphics, Wi-Fi or a recently installed driver).
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_cpu_raised_: The CPU raised a trap the kernel could not handle (often a stack overflow). Leads: CPU overclock/undervolt, RAM, very low-level driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.an_unhandled_ex: An unhandled exception in kernel mode. Parameter 2 is the faulting address. Third-party driver or unstable RAM.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_cpu_detecte: The CPU detected a fatal hardware error (older equivalent of WHEA). Overclock, voltage, temperature or motherboard.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_did_no: A driver did not respond during sleep or wake. Very common with Wi-Fi, USB and graphics drivers; Fast Startup often makes it worse.
engine.bug_check_catalog.internal_power_: Internal power-management error, often tied to hibernation or Fast Startup.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_tried_: A driver tried to write to read-only memory: buggy or malicious driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_misuse: A driver misused kernel memory (double free, bad size). Almost always software.
engine.bug_check_catalog.windows_driver_: Windows Driver Verifier caught a driver misbehaving. If you enabled it, turn it off (verifier /reset) after noting the culprit.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_corrup: A driver corrupted kernel memory. Parameter 4 points into the driver that touched it.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_access: A driver accessed invalid memory at a critical moment. Parameter 4 points into that driver: network (Realtek, Killer, Intel), audio or USB most often.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_graphics_dr: The graphics driver got stuck waiting for the card. Predecessor of TDR: GPU driver, power or overheating.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_process_windo: A process Windows cannot live without stopped. Corrupted system files, SSD dropping out (NVMe) or overzealous antivirus.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_critical_proc: A critical process was terminated, often because the system disk stopped responding (SSD, cable, controller).
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_tried_: A driver tried to execute code from non-executable memory: buggy driver or memory corruption.
engine.bug_check_catalog.fatal_error_in_: Fatal error in the USB stack: faulty USB device, hub or USB controller driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_cpu_core_stop: A CPU core stopped responding. Almost always hardware: CPU overclock/undervolt, voltage, old BIOS, failing CPU.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_kernel_dete: The kernel detected forbidden changes to its structures (PatchGuard): cheat or low-level monitoring driver, or failing RAM.
engine.bug_check_catalog.internal_video_: Internal video memory management error: graphics driver, unstable VRAM (GPU memory overclock) or HAGS.
engine.bug_check_catalog.windows_graphic: Windows' graphics kernel (DirectX) hit a fatal error, often after a botched GPU driver update.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_graphics_ca: The graphics card stopped responding and Windows could not restart its driver. GPU driver, MPO, aggressive undervolt/overclock, power supply or PCIe cable. Parameter 2 points into the graphics driver.

engine.bug_check_catalog.the_graphics_sc: The graphics scheduler detected an inconsistency: GPU driver, HAGS or card overclock.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_hardware_re: The hardware reported an uncorrectable error: CPU (overclock, undervolt, Curve Optimizer), RAM, PCIe link or power supply. Not a driver problem.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_memory_page_w: A memory page was corrupted by hardware: failing or unstable RAM.
engine.bug_check_catalog.a_driver_hogged: A driver hogged the CPU for too long. Classics: old NVMe SSD firmware, storage/SATA driver, audio or network driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_kernel_dete: The kernel detected corruption of its data structures (buffer overrun). Third-party driver, anti-cheat or unstable RAM.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_kernel_heap: The kernel heap was corrupted by a driver. Often a graphics, audio or RGB device driver.
engine.bug_check_catalog.fatal_usb_3_dri: Fatal USB 3 driver error: device, hub, cable or USB power saving.
engine.bug_check_catalog.the_compressed_: The compressed memory store hit an error, often because of the disk (SSD dropping out, bad sectors) or an antivirus.
